What about pointer types?

They're also scalar types!

https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/named_req/ScalarType

Explicit declaration should always take priority, but I'm not 100% sure if that will also capture edgecases like `cvref` equivalents. Granted, if it doesn't, then that's a hole that exists for basically all the other templates too. Either way, I'll prooobably include that in a future rebase, even if I'm not sold on it being necessary

Are these stubs still needed? If they are not used in the codebase (you seem to have removed a lot of them), maybe an [explicit deprecation](https://stackoverflow.com/a/29297970/730797) would be good?
I guess this case is valid for both MSVC and emscripten? Do they not mangle names? Do we have any guarantees that this works for other compilers?
Is there a guarantee that this works even if the binary is obfuscated? I guess obfuscation may introduce other problems too, but just a thought.

Interesting generalized approach! Two comments:

1) While the source code doesn't currently differentiate anyway, we may want to use the appropriate `operator()` based on the actual enum type (`std::underlying_type_t<T>`).
2) This is opening a new can of worms for implicit conversions, where previously only `Side` and `Orientation` were allowed. Perhaps we can make this explicit, and re-add `Side` and `Orientation` back as implicit for backwards compat (for now)?

Do these 3 cases have to be separate? I don't really see a difference.

GCC and Clang are the main two compilers that return mangled names from `typeid`[^1]. I *believe* emscription falls into the same camp as clang, but I'm not 100% positive.

[^1]: https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/types/type_info/name#Notes

I suppose not. I kept them for compatibility with third-party modules, but their removal isn't technically "breaking" unless you do a deliberate rescope like `RenderingDevice`. Will likely remove next rebase.
No clue. I'll dig for alternative ways of grabbing typenames natively just in case

1. All int-likes are cast to/from `int64_t` with Variant as-is, so that being the baseline should be fine (or, at least, working-as-expected).
2. For better or for worse, Variant is built upon implicit casts. Those two were specified before for convenience, in a manner camp to the non-packed `Vector<>` overloads; I wouldn't consider that *excluding* other enums, so much as not wanting to deal with extra verbosity. In other words: this won't break compat, as it's not changing any behavior for the existing code.
